claims.text: Selective surface segregation of low-melting-point constituents is the primary governing factor for premelting onset and melting-temperature depression in HEA nanoparticles.
Surface segregation of low-melting-point elements reduces local surface cohesive energy.
Reduced surface cohesive energy creates localized sites for early atomic disordering.
Segregated HEA nanoparticles premelt earlier than compositionally homogeneous nanoparticles and bulk HEAs.
The proposed initial particles are near-equiatomic, 5–20 nm HEA nanoparticles with largely homogeneous elemental distributions immediately after synthesis.
Mild post-synthesis annealing under an inert atmosphere can promote or suppress surface segregation relative to a passivated, chemically homogenized reference.
The relevant structural mediator is a surface-enriched layer a few atomic layers thick that preferentially contains the lower-melting-point constituents.
Thermodynamic driving forces cause low-melting-point elements to segregate to nanoparticle surfaces in order to minimize total free energy.
Surface-localized disorder provides nucleation sites for subsequent bulk melting.
Pronounced surface segregation is predicted to lower the premelting onset by tens of degrees relative to surface-homogenized nanoparticles.
Pronounced surface segregation is predicted to lower the premelting onset relative to bulk HEA samples.
The predicted segregation–premelting relationship should hold over the 5–20 nm particle-size range.
The predicted relationship should hold for HEAs whose constituents have substantially different elemental bulk melting points.
Bulk homogeneous HEAs and nanoparticles treated to suppress segregation are expected to have higher premelting-onset temperatures.
The segregation-driven effect may weaken at lower surface-to-volume ratios.
The segregation-driven effect may weaken when the alloying elements have similar melting points.
Premelting onset can be measured through temperature-resolved TEM observations of surface structural fluctuations or local atomic disorder.
A lack of a significant premelting-onset difference between segregated and homogenized particles would falsify the hypothesis.
A lack of correlation between low-melting-element surface enrichment and early structural disordering would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as largely homogeneous immediately after synthesis, whereas the experimental comparison later treats untreated nanoparticles as the segregated condition. The source or treatment that creates pronounced segregation in the untreated arm is therefore internally unclear.
